# Control Narrative: Ammonia Screw Compressor C-101

**Document:** CN-C101, Rev A (draft for review)
**Scope:** Equipment module C-101 and its interfaces to machine room ammonia detection and emergency shutdown
**Platform:** Allen-Bradley CompactLogix PLC; HMI in the engine room office
**Standards basis:** ANSI/ISA-5.06.01 structure, ANSI/ISA-106 states, ASD-STE100 wording

This narrative defines what the system must do. The integrator's software design spec defines how the code does it. All numbers are in the setpoint list (Section 11). Values marked "Confirm" are provisional; the integrator can code them as adjustable parameters and finalize them before FAT.

---

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

C-101 is a 400 hp oil-flooded ammonia screw compressor. It holds machine room suction pressure at setpoint by moving the slide valve. Capacity range is from SP-10 to SP-11.

| Boundary | Interface | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| Upstream | Suction header, measured by PT-101 | Input |
| Downstream | Discharge header, measured by TT-103 (temperature only, see OI-01) | Input |
| Motor | Soft starter SS-101 (across-the-line, no VFD) | Command and status |
| Machine room safety | AE-110A/B, EF-201, XV-120, break-glass HS-130 | Shared with the plant |
| Other compressors | ESD command to all machine room compressors | Output |
| Out of scope | Condensers, evaporators, receivers, defrost, lead/lag between compressors (OI-08) | n/a |

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-001 | C-101 starts only on an operator START command at the HMI. No automatic start or restart exists. | FAT: Cycle PLC power and clear all trips. Verify C-101 stays OFF. Verify no logic path issues a run command without an HMI START. |

## 2. Equipment and tags

No instrument index was supplied. Tags marked "Proposed" are needed for the functions below. The owner or EOR must confirm them in the index (OI-02).

| Tag | Description | Signal | Fail / de-energized state | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C-101 | Screw compressor, 400 hp | n/a | n/a | Given |
| SS-101 | C-101 soft starter: run command (DO), running (DI), at speed (DI), fault (DI), ready/remote (DI) | DO/DI | Run command off = motor stops | Proposed tag |
| PT-101 | Suction pressure | AI 4-20 mA | Bad PV per Section 8 | Given |
| PDT-102 | Oil differential pressure | AI 4-20 mA | Bad PV per Section 8 | Given |
| TT-103 | Discharge temperature | AI 4-20 mA | Bad PV per Section 8 | Given |
| II-104 | C-101 motor current (CT) | AI 4-20 mA | Bad PV per Section 8 | Given |
| ZT-105 | Slide valve position | AI 4-20 mA | Bad PV per Section 8 | Proposed |
| XY-106A | Slide valve LOAD solenoid | DO | De-energized (slide valve holds) | Proposed |
| XY-106B | Slide valve UNLOAD solenoid | DO | De-energized (slide valve holds) | Proposed |
| AE-110A | Machine room NH3 detector A | AI 4-20 mA | Bad PV per Section 8 | Given |
| AE-110B | Machine room NH3 detector B | AI 4-20 mA | Bad PV per Section 8 | Given |
| EF-201 | Emergency exhaust fan, high-speed run command and running status | DO/DI | See OI-05 | Given |
| XV-120 | Machine room main liquid solenoid | DO | De-energized = closed | Given |
| HS-130 | Break-glass emergency shutdown station, outside machine room. Hardwired. PLC reads status (DI, open = ESD). | DI | Open circuit = ESD | Proposed tag |
| YS-140 | ESD command to other machine room compressors (DO, de-energize = shut down) | DO | De-energized = shut down | Proposed |

## 3. States and transitions (ISA-106)

C-101 uses state-based control. Start and stop are sequences inside the STARTING and STOPPING states (Section 5). In RUNNING, capacity mode is AUTO or MANUAL (Section 4).

### 3.1 State table

| State | Description | Entry permissives | Allowed exits | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| OFF | Motor stopped. HMI shows READY when all start permissives (3.2) are true. | Stop sequence complete, or TRIPPED reset, or ESD reset, or PLC power-up | STARTING, TRIPPED, ESD | Manual (operator decides to start) |
| STARTING | Start sequence (Table 5.1) runs. | All start permissives true and operator confirms START | RUNNING, OFF (aborted), STOPPING, TRIPPED, ESD | Operator-prompted, then automatic |
| RUNNING | Motor runs. Capacity control active in AUTO or MANUAL. | Start sequence step 5 complete | STOPPING, TRIPPED, ESD | Automatic (AUTO) or manual (MANUAL) |
| STOPPING | Stop sequence (Table 5.2) runs. | Operator confirms STOP | OFF, TRIPPED, ESD | Operator-prompted, then automatic |
| TRIPPED | Motor stopped by a C-101 trip. First-out cause held. | Any trip cause in Section 6 | OFF (on reset), ESD | Manual reset |
| ESD | Machine room emergency shutdown. Motor stopped, XV-120 closed, YS-140 de-energized. | ESD cause in Section 6 | OFF (on supervisor reset) | Manual reset, supervisor level |

### 3.2 Start permissives (all must be true for READY)

| ID | Permissive |
|---|---|
| P1 | C-101 is not in TRIPPED or ESD. |
| P2 | HS-130 circuit is healthy (closed). |
| P3 | Starts in the last SP-36 window are fewer than SP-35. |
| P4 | Time since the last stop is more than SP-37. |
| P5 | PT-101 is above SP-17. |
| P6 | TT-103 is below SP-26. |
| P7 | PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104, ZT-105 have no bad-PV status. |
| P8 | SS-101 shows ready/remote and no fault. |
| P9 | AE-110A and AE-110B are both below SP-32 and both healthy. |

### 3.3 Transition table

| ID | From | To | Condition | Initiator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | OFF | STARTING | All P1-P9 true, operator pushes START and confirms | Operator |
| T2 | STARTING | RUNNING | Start sequence step 5 complete | Auto |
| T3 | STARTING | OFF | Step 1 timeout (start aborted before run command) | Auto |
| T4 | STARTING | STOPPING | Operator pushes STOP and confirms (enters Table 5.2 at step 2) | Operator |
| T5 | RUNNING | STOPPING | Operator pushes STOP and confirms | Operator |
| T6 | STOPPING | OFF | Stop sequence step 3 complete | Auto |
| T7 | STARTING, RUNNING, STOPPING | TRIPPED | Any trip cause, Section 6 rows C1-C9 | Auto |
| T8 | TRIPPED | OFF | All trip causes clear and operator pushes RESET | Operator |
| T9 | Any | ESD | ESD cause, Section 6 rows C12-C13 | Auto |
| T10 | ESD | OFF | All ESD causes clear and supervisor pushes ESD RESET | Supervisor |

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-002 | The PLC permits only the transitions in Table 3.3. | FAT: From each state, try each command. Verify only listed transitions occur. |
| FR-C101-003 | The HMI shows READY only when P1-P9 are all true. The HMI shows each failed permissive by name. | FAT: Make each permissive false one at a time. Verify READY clears and the correct permissive shows. |
| FR-C101-004 | The PLC ignores START when READY is false. | FAT: Make P5 false. Push START. Verify no state change. |
| FR-C101-005 | RESET has no effect while any trip cause is still active. | FAT: Hold TT-103 above SP-24. Push RESET. Verify C-101 stays TRIPPED. |
| FR-C101-006 | A trip or ESD in STOPPING goes to TRIPPED or ESD, not OFF. | FAT: Start a stop. Simulate TT-103 above SP-24 during step 1. Verify TRIPPED. |

## 4. Regulatory control

### 4.1 Suction pressure capacity control

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| PV | PT-101 |
| Setpoint | SP-01. Limits SP-02 to SP-03. Supervisor login required to change. |
| Output | Load pulses on XY-106A, unload pulses on XY-106B |
| Action | PT-101 above setpoint: load. PT-101 below setpoint: unload. |
| Position limits | No load pulses at or above SP-11. No unload pulses at or below SP-10 (ZT-105). |
| Tuning | SP-04 to SP-08 are commissioning-adjustable. |

**AUTO mode.** The PLC calculates error as PT-101 minus setpoint. When the error is more than SP-04, the PLC sends one load pulse in each SP-05 period. When the error is less than minus SP-04, the PLC sends one unload pulse in each SP-05 period. Pulse on-time is the error magnitude times SP-06, limited between SP-07 and SP-08. Within the deadband, the PLC sends no pulses.

**MANUAL mode.** The operator pushes LOAD or UNLOAD on the faceplate. Each push gives one pulse of SP-09 on-time. Holding the button does not give continuous output. All overrides in 4.2 stay active in MANUAL.

**Mode changes.** Transfer between AUTO and MANUAL does not move the slide valve. C-101 enters RUNNING in AUTO.

### 4.2 Capacity overrides (highest priority first)

| Priority | Override | Activate | Release | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Trip or ESD | Section 6 | Section 6 | Load off, unload on for SP-43 |
| 2 | High current unload | II-104 at or above SP-29 | II-104 below SP-30 | Block load. Unload pulses at SP-08 on-time each SP-05 period. |
| 3 | Low suction unload | PT-101 at or below SP-13 | PT-101 above SP-14 | Block load. Unload pulses at SP-08 on-time each SP-05 period. |
| 4 | Current load inhibit | II-104 at or above SP-27 | II-104 below SP-28 | Block load. Unload allowed. |
| 5 | Start/stop hold | STARTING or STOPPING state | Sequence step complete | Sequence controls the solenoids |
| 6 | AUTO or MANUAL demand | Normal | Normal | Per 4.1 |

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-010 | In AUTO, PT-101 above SP-01 plus SP-04 gives load pulses on XY-106A. | FAT: Simulate PT-101 above the band. Record XY-106A. Verify pulse period SP-05 and on-time per SP-06, limited SP-07 to SP-08. |
| FR-C101-011 | In AUTO, PT-101 below SP-01 minus SP-04 gives unload pulses on XY-106B. | FAT: As FR-C101-010, unload direction. |
| FR-C101-012 | Within the deadband, XY-106A and XY-106B stay de-energized. | FAT: Simulate PT-101 inside the band for 3 SP-05 periods. Verify no pulses. |
| FR-C101-013 | XY-106A and XY-106B are never energized at the same time. | FAT: Run all test cases with an interlock monitor on both outputs. Verify zero overlaps. |
| FR-C101-014 | Load pulses stop at SP-11. Unload pulses stop at SP-10. | FAT: Simulate ZT-105 at each limit with demand in that direction. Verify no pulse. |
| FR-C101-015 | Only a supervisor login can change SP-01. The PLC rejects values outside SP-02 to SP-03. The HMI logs each change with user and time. | FAT: Try a change as operator (rejected). Try a value outside the limits as supervisor (rejected). Make a valid change and verify the log entry. |
| FR-C101-016 | Each MANUAL push gives one pulse of SP-09. | FAT: Push and hold LOAD. Verify a single pulse. |
| FR-C101-017 | Overrides in 4.2 act in AUTO and MANUAL with the stated priority. | FAT: Simulate each override in each mode. Simulate overrides 2 and 4 at the same time. Verify the higher priority wins. |
| FR-C101-018 | AUTO/MANUAL transfer does not pulse either solenoid. | FAT: Transfer both directions inside and outside the deadband. Verify no pulse at transfer. |
| FR-C101-019 | If ZT-105 does not change by SP-50 after SP-49 consecutive pulses in one direction, the PLC raises alarm A-11. | FAT: Freeze simulated ZT-105 in AUTO with demand. Verify A-11 after SP-49 pulses. |

## 5. Sequences

### 5.1 Start sequence (state STARTING)

Trips C2-C13 are active in all steps. Low oil DP trip C1 and alarm A-01 are bypassed from step 2 transition until SP-22 elapses.

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | HMI asks "Start C-101?" | Operator selects YES | SP-51 | Prompt closes. C-101 stays OFF. |
| 1 | De-energize XY-106A. Energize XY-106B continuously. | ZT-105 at or below SP-12 | SP-38 | Alarm A-12. De-energize XY-106B. Go to OFF. Do not count a start. |
| 2 | Add one start to the start counter. Energize SS-101 run command. | SS-101 running feedback true. Start SP-22 bypass timer. | SP-39 | Trip, first-out "C-101 fail to start" (C9). |
| 3 | Keep XY-106B energized. | SS-101 at-speed true | SP-40 | Trip, first-out "C-101 fail to reach speed" (C9). |
| 4 | Keep XY-106B energized. | SP-22 bypass timer elapsed | SP-22 (timer end) | Low oil DP trip C1 becomes active. If PDT-102 is at or below SP-20, C1 trips C-101 after SP-21. |
| 5 | De-energize XY-106B. Set capacity mode to AUTO. | Executes in one scan | None (one scan) | None. Go to RUNNING. |

### 5.2 Normal stop sequence (state STOPPING)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | HMI asks "Stop C-101?" | Operator selects YES | SP-51 | Prompt closes. C-101 stays in its state. |
| 1 | Block load. Energize XY-106B continuously. | ZT-105 at or below SP-12 | SP-41 | Alarm A-13. Go to step 2. |
| 2 | De-energize SS-101 run command. Keep XY-106B energized. | SS-101 running feedback false | SP-42 | Alarm A-14 (high priority). Keep run command off. Stay in step 2. |
| 3 | Start SP-37 off timer. De-energize XY-106B after SP-43 from step 2 start. | Executes in one scan | None (one scan) | None. Go to OFF. |

### 5.3 Trip action (used by Section 6)

1. De-energize SS-101 run command at once. Do not unload first.
2. De-energize XY-106A.
3. Energize XY-106B for SP-43, then de-energize it.
4. Latch the first-out cause.
5. Start the SP-37 off timer.

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-020 | Start sequence steps run in the order in Table 5.1. Each step gives its failure response at its timeout. | FAT: Run a normal start. Then fail each step's transition condition. Verify timeout value and response. |
| FR-C101-021 | Step 1 timeout does not count as a start. A step 2 entry counts as a start. | FAT: Fail step 1. Verify the start count does not change. Fail step 2. Verify the count increments. |
| FR-C101-022 | C1 and A-01 are inhibited only from step 2 running feedback until SP-22 elapses. | FAT: Hold PDT-102 below SP-20 from the start. Verify no trip before SP-22. Verify trip at SP-22 plus SP-21. |
| FR-C101-023 | Stop sequence steps run in the order in Table 5.2 with stated timeouts and responses. | FAT: Run a normal stop. Then freeze ZT-105 and the running feedback. Verify A-13 and A-14. |
| FR-C101-024 | A trip executes the trip action in 5.3 without unloading first. | FAT: Trip from RUNNING at full load. Verify SS-101 run off in the same scan as the trip. Verify XY-106B on for SP-43. |
| FR-C101-025 | When the start count in the rolling SP-36 window reaches SP-35, P3 blocks START. The HMI shows time until the next allowed start. | FAT: Make SP-35 starts with shortened SP-37. Verify P3 blocks. Verify the countdown and release time. |
| FR-C101-026 | P4 blocks START until SP-37 elapses after any stop or trip. | FAT: Stop C-101. Try START before and after SP-37. |

## 6. Interlocks and permissives (cause-and-effect)

No cause-and-effect chart was supplied. These rows are the chart for C-101. Trip delays are on-delays; the cause must stay true for the full delay.

| Row | Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | PDT-102 at or below SP-20 for SP-21 (not during start bypass) | C-101 trip (5.3) | Latched | Operator RESET at HMI after PDT-102 cause clears (motor stopped, so cause clears when no longer evaluated; reset allowed when C-101 is stopped) |
| C2 | TT-103 at or above SP-24 for SP-25 | C-101 trip | Latched | Operator RESET after TT-103 below SP-24 |
| C3 | PT-101 at or below SP-15 for SP-16 | C-101 trip | Latched | Operator RESET after PT-101 above SP-15 |
| C4 | PT-101 bad PV (Section 8) | C-101 trip | Latched | Operator RESET after PT-101 healthy |
| C5 | PDT-102 bad PV, after start bypass | C-101 trip | Latched | Operator RESET after PDT-102 healthy |
| C6 | TT-103 bad PV | C-101 trip | Latched | Operator RESET after TT-103 healthy |
| C7 | SS-101 fault input | C-101 trip | Latched | Reset SS-101 locally, then operator RESET |
| C8 | SS-101 running feedback lost while run command is on (after step 2) | C-101 trip, first-out "motor stopped unexpectedly" | Latched | Operator RESET |
| C9 | Start sequence step 2 or 3 timeout | C-101 trip | Latched | Operator RESET |
| C10 | II-104 at or above SP-27 | Block load (override 4) | Auto-reset below SP-28 | Automatic |
| C11 | II-104 at or above SP-29 | Block load, force unload (override 2) | Auto-reset below SP-30 | Automatic |
| C11a | PT-101 at or below SP-13 | Block load, force unload (override 3) | Auto-reset above SP-14 | Automatic |
| C12a | AE-110A or AE-110B at or above SP-32 | Alarm A-20. Start EF-201 high speed. | EF-201 run latched | Operator RESET FAN at HMI after both AE-110A/B below SP-32 |
| C12 | AE-110A or AE-110B at or above SP-33 (1-out-of-2, no delay) | ESD: C-101 trip action, de-energize YS-140 (all compressors), de-energize XV-120, EF-201 high speed | Latched | Supervisor ESD RESET after both AE-110A/B below SP-34 |
| C13 | HS-130 open (hardwired break-glass) | Hardwired: open all compressor starter control circuits and XV-120 power, independent of the PLC. PLC: same ESD effects as C12, and EF-201 high speed. | Latched | Reset HS-130 locally, then supervisor ESD RESET |
| C14 | AE-110A or AE-110B bad PV | Alarm A-22. Start EF-201 high speed. | EF-201 run latched | Operator RESET FAN after detector healthy |

**Notes.** XV-120 opens again only after ESD RESET, with an operator OPEN command at the HMI. It does not open automatically on reset. ESD RESET does not start any compressor. C-101 goes to OFF and needs a normal START.

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-030 | Each row C1-C14 gives the stated effect, latch behavior, and reset method. | FAT: Simulate each cause. Verify each effect, the delay, the latch, and that reset works only as stated. |
| FR-C101-031 | The HMI shows the first-out cause for each trip and ESD. Later causes show as subsequent. | FAT: Simulate C2, then C3 one second later. Verify C2 shows first-out. |
| FR-C101-032 | On C12 or C13, the PLC de-energizes SS-101 run, YS-140, and XV-120 within SP-48. | FAT: Simulate AE-110A at SP-33. Measure cause-to-output time on each DO. |
| FR-C101-033 | Either detector alone causes C12 (1-out-of-2). | FAT: Test AE-110A alone, then AE-110B alone. |
| FR-C101-034 | HS-130 stops C-101 and closes XV-120 with the PLC in program mode or powered off. | FAT: Put PLC in program mode. Run C-101 on a test starter circuit. Open HS-130. Verify motor stop and XV-120 closed. |
| FR-C101-035 | ESD RESET needs supervisor login and both detectors below SP-34. XV-120 stays closed until an operator OPEN command. | FAT: Try reset as operator (rejected). Try reset with AE-110A above SP-34 (rejected). Reset validly. Verify XV-120 stays closed. |

### 6.1 Relation to SIS

No function in this narrative is credited as a safety instrumented function. The BPCS trips above give equipment protection. HS-130 is a hardwired code-required emergency shutoff, independent of the PLC. If the hazard review (OI-04) credits any function as a SIF, specify it in an IEC 61511 SRS and reference that SRS here.

| ID | Tag | Alarm | Setpoint / delay | Priority | Operator response |

| A-04 | TT-103 | Discharge temperature high trip | C2 | High | Find cause before reset. |

| A-06 | PT-101 | Suction pressure low trip | C3 | High | Check evaporator loads and liquid feed before reset. |
| A-07 | II-104 | Current limit, load inhibited | C10 | Low | No action unless it continues. Check discharge pressure. |
| A-08 | II-104 | Current high, force unload | C11 | Medium | Check discharge pressure and motor. |

|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-040 | Each alarm A-01 to A-25 activates at its stated condition and shows on the HMI alarm summary. | FAT: Simulate each condition. Verify alarm text, priority, and time stamp. |
| FR-C101-041 | A-01 is inhibited during the start bypass (SP-22). | FAT: Covered in FR-C101-022. |

## 8. Abnormal handling

### 8.1 Bad PV

A signal is bad when it is below SP-44 or above SP-45 for SP-46, or when its I/O module reports a fault.

| Tag | Response to bad PV |
|---|---|
| PT-101 | Trip C-101 (C4). Low suction protection is lost. |
| PDT-102 | Trip C-101 after the start bypass (C5). During the bypass, hold the start. Trip at bypass end if still bad. |
| TT-103 | Trip C-101 (C6). |
| II-104 | Block load. Unload allowed. Alarm A-09. No trip. Motor overload protection stays in SS-101. |
| ZT-105 | Block load in AUTO and MANUAL. Unload allowed. Alarm A-09. Blocks the next start (P7). |
| AE-110A/B | Start EF-201 high speed. Alarm A-22 (C14). The healthy detector still gives C12. |

### 8.2 Communication loss

| Event | Response |
|---|---|
| HMI to PLC | The PLC keeps the present state, mode, and setpoint. All trips and ESD stay active. HMI shows A-24 after SP-47. No state change on restore. |
| PLC to I/O module | All inputs on that module go bad (8.1). All outputs on that module go to their de-energized state (8.3). |

### 8.3 Power loss, restart, and fail positions

| Event | Response |
|---|---|
| PLC fault or program mode | All PLC outputs de-energize. C-101 stops. XV-120 closes. YS-140 de-energizes (other compressors shut down). HS-130 stays functional. |
| PLC power restored | C-101 starts in OFF. No automatic restart. Trip and ESD latches are retained through power loss. Start count is retained. SP-37 off timer restarts from zero. Alarm A-25. |
| Motor power lost, PLC on | C8 trips C-101. |

| Output | De-energized / fail state |
|---|---|
| SS-101 run command | Off (motor stops) |
| XY-106A, XY-106B | Off (slide valve holds position) |
| XV-120 | Closed |
| YS-140 | Shut down other compressors |
| EF-201 high-speed command | See OI-05 |

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-050 | Each bad PV gives the response in 8.1. | FAT: Inject below SP-44 and above SP-45 on each AI. Verify response after SP-46. |
| FR-C101-051 | HMI comms loss does not change C-101 state, mode, or setpoint. | FAT: Disconnect the HMI with C-101 running in AUTO. Verify control continues. Simulate C2. Verify trip. |
| FR-C101-052 | On PLC power-up, C-101 is OFF, trip/ESD latches and start count are retained, and A-25 shows. | FAT: Trip C-101, cycle PLC power. Verify all items. |
| FR-C101-053 | All outputs go to the fail state in 8.3 on PLC program mode and on module fault. | FAT: Force each condition. Measure each output. |

## 9. Operator interface

**C-101 faceplate shows:** state, capacity mode, READY and each failed permissive, PT-101, setpoint, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104 in % FLA, ZT-105, load/unload solenoid status, start bypass countdown, starts used in the window, time to next allowed start, first-out cause, active overrides.

**Machine room safety display shows:** AE-110A/B values and health, EF-201 command and running status, XV-120 command and position status, HS-130 status, ESD state and first-out.

| Action | Access | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| START, STOP | Operator | "Start C-101?" / "Stop C-101?" YES/NO |
| AUTO/MANUAL, LOAD, UNLOAD | Operator | None |
| Trip RESET, RESET FAN | Operator | "Reset C-101 trip?" YES/NO |
| Setpoint SP-01 | Supervisor | Shows old and new values. Confirm. |
| ESD RESET | Supervisor | "Reset machine room ESD? XV-120 stays closed." YES/NO |
| XV-120 OPEN | Operator, only after ESD reset | "Open main liquid XV-120?" YES/NO |

| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-060 | The faceplate and safety display show every item listed above. | FAT: Check each item against this list with live simulation. |
| FR-C101-061 | Each action in the table needs the stated access level and prompt. | FAT: Try each action at each access level. |
| FR-C101-062 | Operations signs off states (Section 3), prompts, and displays before FAT. | Document review: signed sign-off sheet. |

## 10. Open items

### Notes for the reviewer

- **Most important gap:** OI-01. The process data gives no high discharge pressure protection. Resolve this before the integrator starts coding.
- **Assumptions that change behavior:** The start bypass is timed from running feedback. Bad PT-101, PDT-102, or TT-103 trips C-101; bad II-104 only blocks load. XV-120 needs a separate OPEN command after ESD reset. Each of these is in the open items so operations and the EOR can overrule them.
- **STE pass:** Narrative and step text is written to STE limits. Requirement tables use short descriptive sentences. Do a final STE edit after the open items close and values are confirmed.
- **Change control:** After construction starts, change this document only through MOC with revision clouds and a change log.
